Yes, the story has an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. 

The writer effectively uses summary and exposition in the opening paragraphs to compress ten years of history, establishing who Q was in college—effortlessly competent, charming, and seemingly untroubled—and how the narrator idolized him. This background information is essential for the central real-time scene at the municipal pool to have emotional weight. During the pool scene, the story slows down into real-time dialogue and action, allowing the reader to witness Q faltering and failing in a difficult conversation, directly contrasting the exposition about his past. Finally, the story uses brief summary to reflect on the encounter and closes with a short, grounding scene at the pool a week later. Both elements work together seamlessly to maintain pacing and deliver the story's emotional arc.
